Cards Total | 154 |- ! Card Size | 63x88mm |} '''Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy''' is the 28th Star Wars CCG product, published by Decipher on 10 January 2001. It is 154 cards (77 per side): 34 very rare foils, 62 super rare foils, 4 ultra rare foils, and 54 premium cards, plus five foil box/case toppers. Packs are 18 cards, MSRP $4.95, 30 packs per box. Each pack has '''one foil''' from the list below, two unique premiums (listed under Card list), and random reprints. Those reprints are not listed. Some packs did not contain a Japanese card. A foil of a title that is not on this list (and is not one of the box/case toppers) is not a Decipher Reflections II pack foil.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2]. Yeah, I couldn't believe it either. The Sakiyan bounty hunter is an underused powerhouse, for fairly obvious reasons. Ability = 4 is one big reason: any card that draws battle destiny on its own speaks for itself. Add to that [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]'s immunity to attrition < 3, and you've got a guy who can draw his own destiny AND potentially avoid falling victim to the attrition of his enemies. Can you think of any other characters with such abilities? Do the names [[Darth Vader]], [[Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], or [[Princess Leia]] ring a bell? Djas does appear to have one glaring weakness upon first glance: Power = 1, but take another look at his game text: Power +1 for each DS icon present, +2 under "nighttime conditions." Ouch...drop [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]] at any DS location with two DS icons, and he's Power = 3. Add a [[Presence Of The Force]], and he's Power = 4. Make that DS location the [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]], and he's Power = 5. Play [[Sunsdown]] on [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]...forget about it...Power = 8...my man is ragin': "The [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] is MY house!!!" But it doesn't end there: this guy is rife with combo potential. Let's go back to his Ability = 4. Not only can he utilize the Dark Jedi abilities of [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]] and [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] with some proficiency, but also: can you say, "[[Weapon Levitation]]?" That's right: "I'll take that lightsaber, Mr. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Kenobi]]." What's that? You say you don't use [[Weapon Levitation]]? (Well, you should!) Just give Djas (a warrior, by the way) his own [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]]...only 3 Force to deploy and target (much less than most DS characters), and he has as much chance to hit Rebels and their co-conspirators as [[Lord Vader]] himself. The lightsaber combos that follow go without saying ([[All Too Easy]], [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]], [[You Are Beaten]], etc., etc.). Also, want to add a little extra attrition to your damage with [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]? Try [[Res Luk Ra'auf]], adding a battle destiny for a bounty hunter defending alone, giving Djas and his Ability = 4 not one, but TWO battle destiny draws. This list goes on, but you get the picture...[[Djas Puhr]], Sakiyan bounty hunter, ROCKS. He is a must in most DS ground decks and can really show his stuff when the LS spreads their forces thin to force drain and leaves characters with less than Ability = 4 at a site. Next time you need some hired ground muscle (and one heck of a tracker), call on [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]. Combos: Djas + [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] + [[Presence Of The Force]] = Power of 5, Immunity to Attrition < 3, and a destiny draw.
